newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urges re-doubled bid to reach airline deal.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges re-doubled bid to reach airline deal.

text.p: President Bill Clinton early on Saturday urged American Airlines and its pilots to re-double their efforts to reach a contract deal, minutes after he intervened to stop a short-lived strike by pilots.

In a statement announcing he was setting up an emergency board to work out a solution to the tussle over pay and conditions, Clinton said: "I urge the parties to continue to use the National Mediation Board and the Presidential Emergency Board to redouble their efforts to reach an agreement."
"A strike would cause a severe disruption to both domestic and international air transportation ... It would be extremely difficult for other carriers to fill the void," Clinton said.
"I was also particularly concerned that a strike would be especially disruptive over a holiday weekend, when hundreds of thousands of citizens rely on our air transit system."
Monday Feb. 17 is Presidents' Day, a federal holiday that many Americans take as a long weekend.
